[
1
]

ATTENDU
que
l'audition des mesures accessoires a eu lieu

les 18 et 19 juin 2009;

[
2
]

ATTENDU
que les
parties demandaient qu'un jugement de divorce soit prononcé;

[
3
]

ATTENDU
que les
motifs du jugement sur les mesures accessoires mentionnent qu'un divorce sera
prononcé à la demande des parties;

[
4
]

ATTENDU
que les
conclusions du jugement sur les mesures accessoires

du 23 juin 2009 omettent toutefois de prononcer le divorce;

[
5
]

ATTENDU
qu'il est
dans l'intérêt de la justice que le jugement soit rectifié aux fins d'ajouter

6
]

7

8

sans

Droit de la famille — 091497

2009 QCCS 2821

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE
OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

LAVAL

No:

540-12-014150-080

DATE:

JUNE 23, 2009

______________________________________________________________________

IN THE PRESENCE OF:

THE HONOURABLE

SYLVIANE BORENSTEIN, J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

K. R.

Plaintiff

v.

M. V.

Defendant

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

[1]

The parties have lived apart for more than one
year, the Court will pronounce their divorce.

[2]

Pursuant to interim orders and a judgment on
provisional measures, which she has appealed, the mother has had custody of the
two daughters 7½ and 9½ years old.

[3]

The father was asking for joint custody but is
now asking for custody to prevent further harm to his daughters and their
relationship with him.

[4]

The mother has since December 20
th
,
2008 systematically disobeyed every judgment giving the father access to his
daughters and they are :

Judge Macerola, April 23, 2008;

Judge Devito, July 23, 2008

Judge Casgrain, December 18, 2008, under appeal;

Judge Trahan, January 14, 2009

Judge Caron, February 4, 2009;

Judge Fournier, March 20, 2009, under appeal.

[5]

Since December 20
th
, the father has
seen his daughters once, the weekend of March 27
th
and spoken to
them only a few times, despite the orders allowing him to speak daily.

[6]

Until December 20
th
, 2008, the father
had regular access to his daughters pursuant to an interim consent signed April
23
rd
, 2008, whereby he had the children every Tuesday and Thursday
5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. and every Saturday from noon to Sunday 6:00 p.m., which
was later extended to 8:00 p.m.

[7]

On December 18, 2008, Justice Casgrain, on
provisional measures, granted the father three consecutive weekends out of
four, from Friday nights to Sunday nights, plus one week during the Christmas
holidays (his choice of week) to go to Acapulco with his daughters, one half of
the school break and Easter holidays (his choice of days), one month during the
summer holidays consisting of two non consecutive weeks.

[8]

Justice Casgrain also ordered the mother to
depart from the family residence by February 27, 2009 at the latest, since it
belongs to the paternal grandmother and the father wants to move back in the
house to receive his children.

[
9
]

Even though Justice Trahan, on January 14, 2009,
maintained Justice Casgrain's judgment, the father was prevented from having
the girls during the Christmas holidays or for the weekends.

[
10
]

Justice Caron, on February 4, 2009, ordered that
the father pick-up the children at school on Fridays at 2:45 p.m. and
reiterated that the mother make all efforts to assure that the father exercise
his access.

[
11
]

In order to prevent the father's access, the
mother, as appears from the Centre Jeunesse de Laval reports DM-34, on February
13, hid in the hallway of the school. When the girls saw their father, they
started screaming. The school nurse asked Mrs R. why she was letting them
scream and she answered, things were supposed to happen that way.

[
12
]

After that date, Mrs R. did not send the girls
to school on Fridays, nor on Thursday April 9
th
, date of the Jewish
holiday, the girls were to be with their fathers.

[
13
]

On March 20
th
, 2009, Justice Fournier
found Mrs R. guilty of contempt of Court for not having obeyed the various
judgments on access and having prevented the father from having his children
since December 2008. He condemned her to seven days in jail but stayed the
execution unless Mrs R. was found guilty of contempt in matters relating to
custody and access within the next year.

[
14
]

Mrs R., still, prevented access and did not send
the children to school on Fridays except for the Friday following Justice
Fournier's judgment, March 27
th
, before inscribing in  appeal, when
the father was able to have the children for a weekend. He has not been able to
see them since and Mrs R. declared to the social worker, Stéfanie Bélanger, who
testified in Court and wrote it in her report (DM-34), that she didn't care
about the seven days in jail she was facing.

[
15
]

Ms Bélanger concluded that : «
it was remarkable to us, the lengths Mrs R.
goes to in order to prevent her daughters from seeing their father, yet she is
convinced she does this to protect them.
»

[
16
]

A psychosocial report signed December 19, 2008,
before the mother prevented access, recommended joint custody but already
suspected what did happen.

[
17
]

At page 6 of the report :
«
… we also observed the mother
prompting the children especially X, to inform us of their discomfort, during
their visits at their father's home …
»

[
18
]

At page 12 :

« … The father appears to be very
caring towards his children … We were impressed with the devotion he
demonstrated towards his daughters. We have no concerns regarding his
attachment and interest towards his children, nor do we believe he would
deliberately harm them. In fact we were impressed with the efforts he made to
have a more meaningful relationship with them. His mother appears to be
supporting him in his quest for shared custody of his children … »

[
19
]

At page 13 :

« … Contrary to what they told us
in their mother's presence we did not find that they were in any way afraid of
their father and their grandmother or not happy in their presences. We believe
that these children are caught in a conflict between two warring parents. We
were surprised however with the lack of affect demonstrated by them when they
described the break up of their family. They impress as not having completed
the mourning process, which could be detrimental to their development in the
future. Furthermore they appear to be more concerned about their mother's
feelings than about their own. There are elements of parentification in their
behaviour that would be detrimental to them in the future. So far it has not
affected them but there are no guarantees that this will continue if the
conflict is not resolved in some manner.

We believe that the children should
benefit from living with their father on a regular basis, as a meaningful
relationship with him will have beneficial effects on the development of the
children, in the short and long term … »

[
20
]

At the end of the hearing of June 17
th
,
the Court ordered that the father pick-up the children from school and bring
them to Court on the morning of the 18
th
as the mother had asked
that the Court meet with the children.

[
21
]

The father was crying as it would be his first
visit since March 27
th
.

[
22
]

On the 18
th
, the Court saw the
children separately. As Stéfanie Bélanger observed in her interviews of the
children, Y was more forthcoming and positive. She told the Court that when
visiting with their father, they have fun.

[
23
]

She enthusiastically described her visit ordered
by the Court on June 17
th
with her father, the 1
st
since
March 27
th
. She slept there and even said she had a good dream. X's
behaviour was similar to the one described by Ms Bélanger. She continuously
rocked back and forth in her chair. She wanted to show the Court what her sister
had written on previous occasions and when asked to talk, she wanted to refer
to what she had written. But when the Court insisted that she speak without
reading, she had little to say.

[
24
]

When speaking about her father, she would only
refer to him as he even after the Court suggested she call him Dad or father.
She said her father had kicked her in pool wearing goggles so it could not be
an accident.

[
25
]

When Mrs R. was asked to name three things the
father brings to the benefit of the children, she remained silent.

[
26
]

With the proof adduced including Stéfanie
Bélanger's reports (DM-34) and her testimony at trial, the Court is convinced
that Mrs R. is presently a danger to her children. She has started a process of
parental alienation, which has to be interrupted immediately before she
succeeds.

[
27
]

It is important that the children be in therapy
and with their father and have no polluting contact with their mother until the
therapist decides that contact with their mother is in the best interest of the
children.

[
28
]

In the meantime, hopefully, the mother will be
in therapy to help her realize the harm she was inflicting on her children and
prepare her for a beneficial relationship with her children in the future.

[
29
]

The house in which the children live since their
birth belongs to their paternal grandmother and is the house in which the
father was brought up.

[
30
]

By consent signed in April 2008, a judgment was rendered, whereby Mrs R. was to leave the house within four months, she did not.

[
31
]

By judgment of December 18, 2008, Mrs R. was
ordered to vacate the house by February 27, 2009, she did not.

[
32
]

The Court, on June 18
th
, at the end
of the trial, by interim order to be valid until this judgment is rendered,
ordered Mrs R. to vacate the premises by July 1
st
, so that the
children can reintegrate their home with their father who has been living with
his mother and receiving the children there. Mrs R. can, similarly, live with
her mother until she finds a place.

[
33
]

Mrs R. is 40 years old and was a saleslady when
she met Mr V.. She is bilingual and has a CEGEP diploma. She has been a
bookkeeper at her mother in law's company since 1993 and continued to do so
from home after her children were born. She was paid a salary and furnished a
car with all its expenses paid.

[
34
]

The company terminated her employment in the
summer of 2008.

[
35
]

On July 23
rd
, 2008, she was ordered
by Justice Devito
: «
Orders
the mother to undertake immediate steps to obtain gainful employment.
»

[
36
]

On December 18
th
, 2008, Justice
Casgrain, after granting Mrs R. spousal support, stated at paragraph 44 of his
judgment :
«
Plaintiff,
however, needs to show to the Court that she will continue making serious
efforts to obtain gainful employment otherwise alimony may be terminated.
»

In his conclusions he :
«

Orders Plaintiff to notify Defendant as soon as she
finds herself a job, along with the details of this job
.
»

[
37
]

At trial, she admitted not having made any
serious efforts to find a job since Justice Casgrain's judgment.

[
38
]

Mrs R.'s credibility has been affected by the
contradictions in her testimony regarding the alleged violence of the father
towards the children, and her producing bogus jewelry bills with the names of
the jewelers erased. However, the Court will set Mr V.'s earnings taking into
consideration the benefits he gets from his mother's company for which he
works, such as split income and car. Also, the Court will add the benefits he
gets from his mother directly, such as living in the house free of charge and
with some of the expenses paid as detailed in DM-32.

[
39
]

Justice Casgrain had estimated Mr V.'s revenues
at $100,000 a year, the Court agrees with that estimate.

[
40
]

The father will be looking after the children's
needs, which will include therapy and babysitters to permit him to work.

[
41
]

The Court will grant Mrs R. spousal support in the
amount of $1,000 a month, starting July 1
st
, only if she has left
the house and remitted the keys to the owner Mrs V.. Her present spousal
support is cancelled as of July 1
st
, 2009.

[
42
]

She will also receive $1,200 for moving
expenses, once she is out of the house.

[
43
]

Her spousal support will be augmented to $1,800
a month upon proof that she has moved into her own dwelling and she produces a
signed lease.

[
44
]

The family patrimony to be divided consists of
furniture and RRSP's.

[
45
]

When the parties moved into Mrs G. V.'s home, it
was fully furnished. Later on, the parties bought some furniture, which Mrs R.
evaluates at $10,000 and Mr V. at $4,000. It is improbable that the furniture
bought by the parties is worth $10,000 today. The Court will fix its value at
$7,300, thus $3,650 will be owed to Mrs R. for the furniture.

[
46
]

As to the RRSP's, Mrs R. has $37,753.87 (R-6)
and Mr V. has $80,124.41$ from which must be deducted $28,645.75, which he
owned previous to the marriage, (DM-12) thus leaving $51,478.66 to be shared
with Mrs R..

[
47
]

All RRSP's total $89,232.53 ÷ 2 = $44,616.26 is
each party's share.

[
48
]

Since Mrs R. only has $37,753.87 in her name, Mr
V. will have to roll over $6,862.39 from his RRSP's to Mrs R.'s.

[
49
]

He will also have to pay her $3,650 for her
share in the furniture.

[
50
]

As to the partnership of acquests, DM-17 shows
Mr V.'s Canadian Savings Bonds, but only $5,700 were purchased after the
marriage. On the other hand, DM-28 shows that Mrs R. had $13,000 in her bank
account in 2008.

[
51
]

Thus an amount of $18,700 is to be split
entitling each party to $9,350. Mrs R. owes Mr V. $3,650.

[
52
]

As to Mrs R.'s other claims, regarding the
family residence or compensatory allowance, they are not founded.

FOR THESE
REASONS, THE COURT :

GRANTS
custody of the minor children to the father as of June 18
th
,
2009;

ORDERS
that there be no contact between the children and the mother except
through emails until the children's therapist decides otherwise in the best
interest of the children;

ORDERS
the mother to prepare the children's clothes to be ready to be
picked-up at the house at 10:00 a.m. Sunday, June 21
st
, 2009;

ORDERS
the mother not to be in the vicinity of the children, keeping a
distance of at least 500 metres until otherwise decided by the children's
therapist;

ORDERS
the father to bring the children to the therapist as soon as the
therapist is available, hopefully in the week of June 22
nd
, 2009;

ORDERS
the mother to leave the premises at [...] in Town A, by July 1
st
,
2009, 10:00 a.m. and
ORDERS
that she be removed by huissiers if she has
not complied;

ORDERS
the mother not to harm the house or its contents;

ORDERS
the mother to remit the keys to the house on July 1
st
,
2009 at 10:00 a.m.;

ORDERS
the father to move in the house with the children on July 1
st
,
2009 at 10:00 a.m. and remit the sum of $1,200 as moving expenses to the mother
upon her complying with her removal, not having caused any damage to the house
and its contents and having handed over the keys;

Strongly
SUGGESTS

to the mother to seek therapy;

ORDERS
the father to pay to Mrs R. after her departure from the house,
spousal support of $1,000 a month to be augmented to $1,800 after she furnishes
proof that she moved into her own dwelling and produces a signed lease;

ORDERS
Mrs R. to actively search for employment under pain of having her
support cancelled;

ORDERS
Mrs R. to notify Mr V. as soon as she finds employment along with
the details concerning it;

ORDERS
the division of the family patrimony;

ORDERS
Mr V. to roll over from his RRSP's into Mrs R.'s RRSP, the sum of
$6,862,39;

ORDERS
Mr V. to pay Mrs R. $3,650 for her share of the furniture;

ORDERS
the dissolution of the partnership of acquests;

ORDERS
Mrs R. to pay to Mr V. $3,650 for his share in the partnership of
acquests;

ORDERS
the partition of the parties' deposits in the Quebec Pension Plan;

ORDERS
provisional execution notwithstanding any appeal;

THE WHOLE
without costs.
